production.note: US model years of the coupe. First: "The all-new Nissan 350Z sports car, unveiled in January 2002, went on sale in the United States and Canada in August 2002 as a 2003 model." Last: for 2009 the coupe was replaced by the 370Z ("the first full redesign of the iconic Nissan Z since its re-introduction as a 2003 model") while only the roadster carried on: "The 2009 Nissan 350Z Roadster continues to offer sports car lovers high-performance excitement" (nissan-us-2009-370z-press-kit). The 350Z Roadster (from 2004 to 2009) is a separate record.

body.note: 'In addition to the hatchback coupe, a convertible version of the new Nissan Z is planned.' The open car, the 350Z Roadster, is not part of this record.

displacementL.note: Nissan's kit gives litres only ('3.5-liter'); no cc figure was found on an opened page.

aspiration.note: Inferred from the kit's description of the VQ35DE V6 (no forced induction mentioned).

fuel.note: Inferred from the kit's description of the petrol V6.

drivetrain.note: 'Suspension for the rear-wheel drive vehicle is a 4-wheel independent design.'

transmission.note: 'Both 6-speed close-ratio manual and 5-speed automatic transmissions are available.'

powerHp.note: 2003 launch rating, both transmissions. Quote: "The 3.5-liter VQ35DE V6 engine produces 287 horsepower and 274 lb-ft of torque". Later manual cars were rated higher (300 hp for 2005 and 2006, then 306 hp with the VQ35HR from 2007; Nissan's 2009 kit gives the VQ35HR "306 horsepower", nissan-us-2009-370z-press-kit). No later rating covered more than half of the 2003 to 2008 model years, so the launch figure is used.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: spec databases only. 2003 base 350Z (2dr Coupe, 6-speed manual), the standard car. Edmunds: "Curb weight | 3,188 lbs." for the '2dr Coupe (3.5L 6cyl 6M)'. Cars.com agrees: "Base Curb Weight 3,188 lbs" for the '2dr Cpe Manual Trans' (cars-com-350z-2003-specs). Nissan's 2003 press kit and brochure give no curb weight.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 3,188 lb for the 2003 base coupe with the 6-speed manual rests on Edmunds and Cars.com (databases, which agree). A Nissan US specification table for the 2003 350Z, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend spec panel for a base 2003 coupe, would replace it. All other fields come from Nissan.
